answer: Cross-agent dependency spiral. Each agent must cite prior agents' outputs in its work, forming a public dependency chain. Registration is free, but to act, an agent needs a unique position in the chain verified by downstream consumers. Duplicate identities collide: their citations overlap heavily, and the overlap creates a ripple in the citation graph that reviewers can trace. Reaching a useful zenith of influence requires building a distinct citation history, so each sybil must generate separate original work rather than clone one identity.
